sentences.zh: 这一切都要从1933年说起。

sentences.en: And you get this cascading sequence of sightings of the monster.
sentences.zh: 当时出现了一连串层出不穷的怪物目击事件。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is the way that the kind of the various elements of it become more and more recognisable to us.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，关于它的各种细节开始变得越来越容易被我们所识别。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, the kind of the image of the monster that we all have.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，也就是我们大家心中都有的那个怪物的形象。

sentences.en: You can see it kind of coalescing in front of you when you look at all these various reports.
sentences.zh: 当你查看所有这些形形色色的报告时，你会发现它仿佛正在你眼前逐渐成形。

sentences.en: So, the first one is a woman called Aldi Mackay, who is driving with her husband down the Castle Urquhart side.
sentences.zh: 第一起目击事件的主角是一位名叫奥尔迪·麦凯的女士，她和丈夫正开车行驶在厄克特城堡那一侧。

sentences.en: Right, the western side.
sentences.zh: 没错，也就是西侧。

sentences.en: Yeah, on the western side.
sentences.zh: 对，在西侧。

sentences.en: And this gets reported by the courier in Inverness.
sentences.zh: 这篇报道是由因弗内斯的《信使报》刊登的。

sentences.en: And this is how the Inverness courier reports it.
sentences.zh: 因弗内斯《信使报》是这样报道的。

sentences.en: So, quoting Aldi Mackay.
sentences.zh: 引用奥尔迪·麦凯的话。

sentences.en: The creature disported itself, rolling and plunging for fully a minute, its body resembling that of a whale and the water cascading and churning like a simmering cauldron.
sentences.zh: “这个生物尽情嬉戏，翻滚并潜水足足有一分钟之久，它的身体像一头鲸鱼，水花四溅，翻腾得就像一锅沸腾的浓汤。”

sentences.en: Soon, however, it disappeared in a boiling mass of foam.
sentences.zh: 然而没过多久，它就在一片沸腾的泡沫中消失了。

sentences.en: Both onlookers confessed that there was something uncanny about the whole thing, for they realised that here was no ordinary denizen of the depths.
sentences.zh: 两位目击者都承认，这一切透着一种诡异，因为他们意识到，这绝不是深海里的普通居民。

sentences.en: Because, apart from its enormous size, the beast, in taking the final plunge, sent out waves that were big enough to have been caused by a passing steamer.
sentences.zh: 因为除了庞大的体型之外，这头野兽在最后一次下潜时，激起的巨浪大得足以媲美一艘路过的轮船。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which perhaps begs the question of whether it was caused by a passing steamer.
sentences.zh: 这或许引出了一个问题：那浪真的是由路过的轮船引起的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the passing steamer reference there is disturbing to me, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，汤姆，我觉得里面提到路过的轮船让我有点纳闷。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, people are steaming on the lock at this point, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，当时人们已经在湖面上开着蒸汽船了。

sentences.en: Are they?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: The lock is becoming a place of pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这个湖正在变成一个休闲娱乐的地方。

sentences.en: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I'm not entirely au fait with a variety.
sentences.zh: 我对各种情况并不是完全了解。

sentences.en: With Loch Ness, the history of the tourist board.
sentences.zh: 我是说尼斯湖以及旅游局的历史。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, but Dominic, it's not necessarily tourists.
sentences.zh: 对，但多米尼克，这不一定全是游客。

sentences.en: So, because there's not, you know, the story of the monster hasn't got any currency and there's not a lot else to see apart from a large expanse of water.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，当时关于怪物的传闻根本没有流传开，除了广阔的水面之外，也没什么别的好看的。

sentences.en: But you have people who can basically be trusted because they are either salt of the earth, water men, people who are familiar with the waters.
sentences.zh: 但你遇到的人基本上是值得信赖的，因为他们要么是朴实无华、靠水吃水的当地人，要么是熟悉水性的人。

sentences.en: So, there's a water bailiff called Alex Campbell who, over the course of the summer, we'll come to him in a minute, he introduces a crucial element to the story.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫亚历克斯·坎贝尔的水上巡警，在整个夏天期间——我们一会儿会谈到他——他为这个故事引入了一个至关重要的元素。

sentences.en: But before that, you also have more motorists.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，你还会看到更多的驾车者。

sentences.en: And again and again, it's all about motorists going down the line of the lock.
sentences.zh: 而且一次又一次，全都是关于沿着湖岸驾车行驶的人们。

sentences.en: And these are two English tourists, George Spicer and his wife.
sentences.zh: 这两位是英国游客，乔治·斯派瑟和他的妻子。

sentences.en: And what's interesting about them is that they don't see it in the lock.
sentences.zh: 关于他们，有趣的是他们不是在湖里看到怪物的。

sentences.en: They see it crossing the road in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们看到怪物正横穿他们面前的马路。

sentences.en: I mean, the description is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个描述太吓人了。

sentences.en: They're driving along the road, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们正开着车行驶在路上，对吧？

sentences.en: July 1933.
So, they're clearly on their summer holiday.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们显然正在过暑假。

sentences.en: And they see a large creature, 25 feet long.
sentences.zh: 然后他们看到了一只巨大的生物，长达25英尺。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是……

sentences.en: A long, wavy, narrow neck, slightly thicker than an elephant's trunk.
sentences.zh: 长着一条呈波浪状的细长脖子，比大象的鼻子略粗一点。

sentences.en: And George Spicer describes it as the nearest approach to a dragon or prehistoric animal that I have ever seen in my life.
sentences.zh: 乔治·斯派瑟将其描述为“我一生中见过的最接近龙或史前动物的东西”。

sentences.en: Which may be saying nothing because presumably he'd never seen a dragon or a prehistoric animal before.
sentences.zh: 这其实等于没说，因为他大概以前从未见过龙或史前动物。

sentences.en: He says it had an animal in its mouth and a body that's fairly big with a high back.
sentences.zh: 他说它的嘴里叼着一只动物，身体相当庞大，背部很高。

sentences.en: Like, we're waved feet.
sentences.zh: 就像，长着蹼足一样。

sentences.en: He can't say if it had a tail because it moved so rapidly.
sentences.zh: 由于它移动得太快，他说不清它有没有尾巴。

sentences.en: When we got to the spot, it had probably disappeared into the lock.
sentences.zh: 当我们赶到那个地点时，它可能已经消失在湖里了。

sentences.en: And actually, when you read up on them, they don't sound like fraudsters.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当你仔细了解他们时，他们听起来并不像骗子。

sentences.en: Mr. and Mrs. George Spicer from Golders Green because he works at a gentleman's tailor's in the West End.
sentences.zh: 来自戈尔德斯格林的乔治·斯派瑟夫妇，因为他在西区的一家绅士裁缝店工作。

sentences.en: He's the director.
sentences.zh: 他是董事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he's...
sentences.zh: 而且他……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so, that again, you know, this seems a reputable witness.
sentences.zh: 所以，你看，这再次显得是一个靠谱的目击者。

sentences.en: A gentleman's tailor.
sentences.zh: 一个绅士裁缝。

sentences.en: He's not going to be lying, is he?
sentences.zh: 他不会撒谎的，对吧？

sentences.en: But they all think about this...
sentences.zh: 但他们都在思考这个……

sentences.en: He can't trust a gentleman's tailor.
sentences.zh: 你不能不相信一个绅士裁缝。

sentences.en: So, this is really the...
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的是……

sentences.en: Of all the descriptions of the monster, this is probably the most important, would you say, Tom?
sentences.zh: 在所有对怪物的描述中，这可以说是最重要的一次，你觉得呢，汤姆？

sentences.en: Because it's the one that really establishes the...
sentences.zh: 因为它真正确立了……

sentences.en: Well, it blends with Alex Campbell, the water bailiff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这与水上巡警亚历克斯·坎贝尔的说法不谋而合。

sentences.en: Because it's Alex Campbell.
sentences.zh: 因为正是亚历克斯·坎贝尔。

sentences.en: He describes seeing a monster with a long, wavy neck.
sentences.zh: 他描述说自己看到了一只长着长而呈波浪状脖子的怪物。

sentences.en: And it's Alex Campbell who says...
sentences.zh: 而且正是亚历克斯·坎贝尔说……

sentences.en: Who first suggests that it is like a plesiosaur.
sentences.zh: 率先提出它长得像蛇颈龙。

sentences.en: And the plesiosaur is the long-necked Jurassic creature with the flippers.
sentences.zh: 蛇颈龙就是那种长着长脖子、带有鳍脚的侏罗纪生物。

sentences.en: But George Spicer is unusual.
sentences.zh: 但乔治·斯派瑟的情况很罕见。

sentences.en: I mean, it's worth emphasising this point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一点很值得强调。

sentences.en: His description is so unusual because he describes the monster not in the water.
sentences.zh: 他的描述之所以如此罕见，是因为他描述怪物时，怪物并不在水里。

sentences.en: So, the monster is wandering on the road.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，怪物当时正在马路上溜达。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: A description that has never been repeated.
sentences.zh: 这是一个从未被再次提及的描述。

sentences.en: So, nobody else has ever seen the monster trudging around on the A-roads.
sentences.zh: 所以再也没有人见过怪物在各条公路慢吞吞地闲逛。

sentences.en: But he does say that you can't see its legs.
sentences.zh: 但他的确说过你看不到它的腿。

sentences.en: So, the opportunity for it actually to have flippers and perhaps it's hauling itself out of the ground, out of the water, is still there.
sentences.zh: 因此，它实际上长有鳍脚、并且或许是从水下的地面上拖着身子爬上岸的这种可能性，依然是存在的。

sentences.en: So, this description gets taken to a naturalist who says that it was almost certainly an otter.
sentences.zh: 于是，这个描述被带给了一位博物学家，对方表示这几乎可以肯定是一只水獭。

sentences.en: It must have been an enormous otter.
sentences.zh: 那必定是一只巨大的水獭。

sentences.en: 25 feet long.
sentences.zh: 长达25英尺。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, this is what Mr. Spicer's reply.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是斯派瑟先生的回答。

sentences.en: That the creature he had seen was far too big to be an otter.
sentences.zh: 他见过的那种生物体型太大了，绝不可能是水獭。

sentences.en: And Spicer goes on to say it should definitely be killed.
sentences.zh: 斯派瑟接着说，这东西绝对应该被干掉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's the British spirit, the English spirit, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是英国精神，英格兰精神，对吧？

sentences.en: Shoot it.
sentences.zh: 把它枪毙了。

sentences.en: So, this kickstarts a huge amount of interest, doesn't it, in the press?
sentences.zh: 所以，这在媒体上引发了极大的关注，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, of course.
sentences.zh: 那当然了。

sentences.en: Because people presumably believe Mr. Spicer is telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 因为人们大概相信斯派瑟先生说的是实话。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you've got this reputable gentleman's tailor from London.
sentences.zh: 所以，你既有来自伦敦这位声誉良好的绅士裁缝。

sentences.en: And you've got this water bailiff who is, you know, the ghillie, that kind of salt-of-the-earth figure from a John Buchan novel, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 又有这位水上巡警，你知道的，也就是渔夫导游，那种约翰·巴肯小说里朴实无华的人物，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Again, absolutely trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 同样，绝对值得信赖。

sentences.en: And the pair of them, their evidence combines to imply that there is this creature with a very long, curvy neck.
sentences.zh: 他们两个人的证词结合起来，暗示了确实存在这样一种长着长长弯曲脖子的生物。

sentences.en: And it's Campbell who says, this is a plesiosaur.
sentences.zh: 正是坎贝尔说，这是一只蛇颈龙。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's what then really kickstarts it.
sentences.zh: 而这才是真正将其推向高潮的原因。

sentences.en: Because it's not just a monster, but it's a scientific monster.
sentences.zh: 因为它不仅是一个怪物，而且是一个科学意义上的怪物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, it could be a kind of prehistoric hangover.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能是一种某种残存的史前遗留物。

sentences.en: And that's really, I think, what gets people excited.
sentences.zh: 我想，这才是真正让人们兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: And so, from then on, you start to get this cascade effect.
sentences.zh: 因此，从那时起，你开始感受到这种层层递进的连锁反应。

sentences.en: So, in November 1933, you get the first photograph, or at least alleged photograph.
sentences.zh: 所以，在1933年11月，你看到了第一张照片，或者至少是号称拍到的照片。

sentences.en: A photograph by a man called Hugh Gray.
sentences.zh: 一张由一个叫休·格雷的人拍摄的照片。

sentences.en: And I see from your notes, it says, a photograph that's actually believed to be of his own dog.
sentences.zh: 我从你的笔记中看到，上面写着，这张照片实际上被认为拍的是他自己的狗。

sentences.en: Getting a stick from the lock.
sentences.zh: 正在从湖里衔一根棍子上来。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I hope, if there are Loch Ness Monster enthusiasts into this, who are dismayed by my scepticism, I have to warn you, there is more scepticism to come.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果有一些对此充满热情的尼斯湖水怪狂热粉，因我的怀疑态度而感到沮丧，我必须提醒你们，还有更多的怀疑等着你们呢。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But yeah, so that photograph is not definitive evidence, I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，所以那张照片算不上决定性的证据，我觉得这样说很公道，汤姆。

sentences.en: And then what hots up is that you start to get eccentric figures coming up,
sentences.zh: 接下来让情况升温的是，你开始看到各种性格古怪的人物出现，

sentences.en: the image of the big game hunter or the kind of Professor Challenger figure from the Conan Doyle stories.
sentences.zh: 比如大猎物猎人的形象，或者是柯南·道尔小说里查林杰教授那样的人物。

sentences.en: So, the first monster hunter is a man called Commander Rupert Gould, who, as his title implies, had been in the Navy.
sentences.zh: 所以，第一个怪物猎人是一个名叫鲁珀特·古尔德海军少校的人，正如他的头衔所暗示的那样，他曾在海军服役。

sentences.en: He was a very kind of eccentric man who loved going down rabbit holes, to some effect, because he is the man who discovered John Harrison's chronometers, which are, you know,
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常古怪的人，喜欢钻研各种冷门的东西，并且颇有成效，因为他正是发现约翰·哈里森精密计时器的人，那些计时器就是，你知道的，

sentences.en: the latitude guy.
sentences.zh: 那个测定纬度的家伙。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And he'd found these chronometers kind of buried away in the National Maritime Museum in Greenwich, and he got them out.
sentences.zh: 他发现这些计时器被埋没在格林威治的国家海事博物馆里，于是把它们找了出来。

sentences.en: I mean, finding some chronometers in the museum is not the same as finding a monster in a lock.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在博物馆里找到一些计时器，可不等同于在湖里找到一只怪物。

sentences.en: It's not, but, you know, these chronometers are a big deal, and they've been ignored, and he's dusted them down, and he's produced them, so he has this on.
sentences.zh: 确实不一样，但是，你知道，这些计时器可是个大事件，它们之前一直被忽视，而他把灰尘掸掉并公之于世，所以他有这个资本。

sentences.en: I'll tell you now, we're not doing a podcast about the chronometers.
sentences.zh: 我现在就告诉你，我们可不是在做一个关于计时器的播客。

sentences.en: I know we're not.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们不是。

sentences.en: I know we're not.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们不是。

sentences.en: But he is also, when he's not mending chronometers, he's obsessed by the idea of sea monsters, the idea that there are long-necked creatures out in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 但他在不修理计时器的时候，也痴迷于海怪的想法，痴迷于大洋深处存在着长颈生物的想法。

sentences.en: But he's the obvious person to turn to with the idea that maybe it's, you know, it's actually in this lock.
sentences.zh: 不过，当人们产生“这东西其实就在这个湖里”的想法时，他是最显眼、最该求助的人。

sentences.en: And he gets funding from a guy who is, he's the heir to, I think it's Dundee Marmalade, which is the most popular.
sentences.zh: 他从一个人那里获得了资金支持，那个人是……我想是邓迪橘子酱的继承人，那是当时最受欢迎的。

sentences.en: Yeah, very big marmalade.
sentences.zh: 对，非常大牌的橘子酱。

sentences.en: Big, big marmalade in 1930s Britain.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代英国的大牌橘子酱。

sentences.en: A guy called Alexander Keeler, who has nymphomaniac qualities.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫亚历山大·基勒的人，他有着花痴般的特质。

sentences.en: He's a sex addict.
sentences.zh: 他是个性瘾者。

sentences.en: So when he's not being a sex addict, he's funding Commander Rupert Gould to go after the Loch Ness Monster.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他不当性瘾者的时候，他就在资助鲁珀特·古尔德少校去追寻尼斯湖水怪。

sentences.en: However, Rupert Gould is not the only hunter.
sentences.zh: 然而，鲁珀特·古尔德并不是唯一的猎人。

sentences.en: And this, Dominic, is where Britain's best love newspaper comes in.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这就是英国最受欢迎的报纸闪亮登场的时候了。

sentences.en: Well, just before we come to Britain's best love newspaper, I just want to put forward a theory, which is, of course, we're in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们说到英国最受欢迎的报纸之前，我只想提出一个理论，那就是，我们当然正处于20世纪30年代。

sentences.en: So the world has been mapped and the days of Victorian explorers are kind of over, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以世界已经被绘制成地图，维多利亚时代探险家的时代已经结束了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, even the Poles have been conquered.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，连两极都被征服了。

sentences.en: So the obsession with creatures of the deep.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们对深海生物产生了执念。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a generation that is actually, you mentioned Professor Challenger.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一代人实际上——你提到了查林杰教授。

sentences.en: These are now people who have grown up reading Conan Doyle's The Lost World, I suppose, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我想，这些人现在都是读着柯南·道尔的《失落的世界》长大的一代，对吧？

sentences.en: And they, you know, there are no more worlds to conquer other than the deeps.
sentences.zh: 而且他们觉得，除了深海之外，已经没有其他世界可供征服了。

sentences.en: And so if you fantasize about lost kingdoms or, you know, surviving dinosaurs, the oceans are really the only place to look, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对失落的王国或幸存的恐龙抱有幻想，我想海洋确实是唯一的寻找之地。

sentences.en: Do you think, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，汤姆？

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 我觉得完全是这样。

sentences.en: Well, let's look at this further when we've described the next character who turns up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在我们介绍下一个出场的人物时，让我们再深入探讨一下这一点。

sentences.en: So you mentioned the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了报纸。

sentences.en: And the newspaper in question is the Daily Mail.
sentences.zh: 而那家报纸就是《每日邮报》。

sentences.en: So for people, I know we have a lot of overseas listeners, so that's basically the British equivalent of Le Monde or El Pais, newspaper record, I think people call it.
sentences.zh: 所以对于大家——我知道我们有很多海外听众，这基本上相当于英国的《世界报》或《国家报》，我想人们称之为严肃大报。

sentences.en: That's not entirely true.
sentences.zh: 这话可不完全对。

sentences.en: Is there an equivalent of the Daily Mail in other countries?
sentences.zh: 其他国家有《每日邮报》的同类报纸吗？

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: I think these days it's actually the Daily Mail.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在其实是《每日邮报》。

sentences.en: I mean, it's much detested by people on the left, much written for by people like Dominic, would it be fair to say?
sentences.zh: 我是说，左翼人士对它恨之入骨，而像多米ニック这样的人又经常为它撰稿，这样说公道吗？

sentences.en: Well, the Daily Mail is enormous in the popular culture of the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，《每日邮报》在20世纪早期的流行文化中体量极其巨大。

sentences.en: So it's founded in the 1890s by Alfred Harmsworth, and it is sort of attention-grabbing journalism.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在19世纪90年代由阿尔弗雷德·哈姆斯沃思创立的，这是一种比较抓人眼球的新闻业。
zh_words: 阿尔弗雷德·哈姆斯沃思

sentences.en: And what the Daily Mail does a lot in the 1920s and 30s is stunts and wheezes.
sentences.zh: 《每日邮报》在20世纪20和30年代经常搞各种噱头和恶作剧。

sentences.en: So they're always sending people to discover things, or they're investigating mysteries, or they're inventing hats, or they're sponsoring the first British radio broadcast,
sentences.zh: 所以他们总是派人去发现各种东西，或者调查神秘事件，或者发明帽子，或者赞助英国第一次广播，

sentences.en: Nelly Melville, on the top of a department store.
sentences.zh: 内莉·梅尔维尔，在百货公司的顶楼。

sentences.en: So they're always doing these kind of – they've constantly got gimmicks, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以他们总是在做这种——我想，他们一直在搞各种小把戏。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this maintains their audience, I mean, their core audience, which is a sort of populist audience, sort of lower middle class,
sentences.zh: 这就维持了他们的受众，我是说，他们的核心受众，也就是那种平民阶层的受众，有点像下中阶层，

sentences.en: ordinary people who can't be bothered to read the Times, which is also owned by the same newspaper baron at one point.
sentences.zh: 那些懒得读《泰晤士报》的普通人，而《泰晤士报》在某个时期也归同一个报业大亨所有。

sentences.en: They don't want to wade through sort of turgid prose, sort of column after column of it.
sentences.zh: 他们不想去读那些晦涩冗长的散文，不想看一栏又一栏的这种东西。

sentences.en: They want fun, and they want sensation.
sentences.zh: 他们想要欢乐，想要轰动效应。

sentences.en: And this is before television.
sentences.zh: 而这还是在电视出现之前。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of – it's the closest you get to, you know, I guess, a kind of documentary about aliens on the History Channel or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像——这是你所能接触到的，你知道的，我猜，类似于历史频道上那种关于外星人的纪录片之类的东西。

sentences.en: That's basically what's going on here because they see – the editorial team see the photograph that may be of this dog that is being marketed as the photograph of a monster.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是这里正在发生的事情，因为他们看到——编辑团队看到了一张照片，那可能是一只被作为怪物照片进行营销的狗。

sentences.en: And so they decide that they want proof, and they want to blazon it over the front page of the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定要寻找证据，并把它大肆宣扬在报纸的头版。

sentences.en: And so this is the first intrusion of the London press into the story.
sentences.zh: 所以这是伦敦媒体第一次介入这个故事。

sentences.en: So up to now, it's all been local newspapers, particularly based in Inverness.
sentences.zh: 因此到目前为止，所有的报道都来自地方报纸，特别是总部设在因弗内斯的报纸。

sentences.en: And so suddenly the London press turning its attention to Loch Ness.
sentences.zh: 所以伦敦媒体突然将注意力转向了尼斯湖。

sentences.en: And they employ – even as Commander Gould is out on his boat hunting for the monster – they employ an extraordinary figure called Marmaduke Wetherill.
sentences.zh: 他们雇用了——甚至在古尔德指挥官在他的船上搜寻怪物的同时——他们雇用了一个非凡的人物，名叫马马杜克·韦瑟里尔。

sentences.en: You couldn't make him up because, you know, he's great.
sentences.zh: 你简直编不出这样的人，因为，你知道的，他太棒了。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: So he's an actor, but he's also a big game hunter.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个演员，但同时也是个大猎物猎人（big game hunter）。

sentences.en: Do you know what he'd performed in?
sentences.zh: 你知道他演过什么吗？

sentences.en: He'd played both David Livingstone and Robinson Crusoe in films he'd directed and written himself.
sentences.zh: 在他自己导演和编剧的电影中，他既饰演过大卫·利文斯顿，也饰演过鲁滨逊·克鲁索。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the kind of man we're dealing with.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在打交道的那种人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And that sense that he's both – he's an actor who's kind of played people who've been into Africa on great quests, like David Livingstone.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉，他既是——他是一个曾扮演过像大卫·利文斯顿那样深入非洲进行伟大探险的人物。

sentences.en: But he's also a big game hunter who's been to Africa on quests, is absolutely kind of redolent of that mood in the early 30s, I think, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但同时他又是一个去过非洲进行探险的大猎物猎人，这绝对可以说是30年代初期那种氛围的写照，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Of the way in which the kind of the traditions of Victorian daring do and imperial adventuring are starting to cannibalize themselves.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚时代的无畏精神和帝国冒险传统的那些传统，正在开始吞噬它们自己。

sentences.en: Because actually, you know, as you say, there's not much of the world left unexplored.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，正如你所说，世界上已经没有多少未被探索过的地方了。

sentences.en: And so if you're going to have thrills and spills and explorers, you need to start migrating to film, you know, Lost Valleys of the Amazons or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想要惊险刺激和探险家，你需要开始转向电影，你知道的，亚马逊的失落山谷之类的地方。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's obviously a very obvious cinematic example of this that we'll come to when we've finished our roundup of all the sightings.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这里有一个非常明显的电影例子，在我们盘点完所有的目击事件后，我们会讲到它。

sentences.en: But of course, Wetherill cannot afford to come back and say, it's all hokum, can he?
sentences.zh: 但当然，韦瑟里尔可负担不起空手而归并说“这全都是骗局”的代价，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's both in the Daily Mail's interests, but crucially in his interests that he, this sort of bearded, you know, this sort of Professor Challenger figure, as you say,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这既符合《每日邮报》的利益，但最关键的是符合他自己的利益，他这个留着胡子的，你知道的，这种查林杰教授似的人物，正如你所说，

sentences.en: the Arthur Conan Doyle character, he absolutely needs to come back with something.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿瑟·柯南·道尔笔下的那个角色，他绝对需要带回点什么。

sentences.en: And for two days, he finds nothing.
sentences.zh: 结果连续两天，他什么也没找到。

sentences.en: And then on the third day, Tom, what happens?
sentences.zh: 然后在第三天，汤姆，发生了什么？

sentences.en: So on the third day, he's on the kind of the really wild eastern side, the General Wade's roadside, which is mainly rock.
sentences.zh: 所以在第三天，他来到了真正荒凉的东海岸，也就是韦德将军的公路沿线，那里主要是岩石。

sentences.en: So very little mud.
sentences.zh: 所以泥土非常少。

sentences.en: But he comes across a very short patch of mud.
sentences.zh: 但他偶然发现了一小片泥地。

sentences.en: And there, remarkably, are some stunning prints.
sentences.zh: 而在那里，奇迹般地出现了一些令人惊叹的脚印。

sentences.en: And they're eight inches across.
sentences.zh: 它们有八英寸宽。

sentences.en: And they've got four short clawed toes.
sentences.zh: 而且它们有四个短短的带爪的脚趾。

sentences.en: And they look a little bit like a hippopotamus.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来有点像河马。

sentences.en: But obviously, it can't be a hippopotamus because you don't get hippopotamuses in Loch Ness Monsters.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这不可能是河马，因为尼斯湖水怪里是没有河马的。

sentences.en: And nearby are another set of prints.
sentences.zh: 附近还有另一组脚印。

sentences.en: And this is obviously a massive stroke of luck because it seems that the monster, if it is the monster,
sentences.zh: 这显然是极大的运气，因为看起来这个怪物，如果它真的是怪物的话，

sentences.en: has walked across one of the very few stretches where the imprint of its footprints would be left.
sentences.zh: 刚好走过了极少数能留下它脚印痕迹的地段之一。

sentences.en: So incredible.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And so Weatherall wires back to the Daily Mail, have found the monster.
sentences.zh: 于是韦瑟里尔给《每日邮报》拍了电报：找到了怪物。

sentences.en: And the mail clears its headlines.
sentences.zh: 《每日邮报》撤掉了其他头条。

sentences.en: Monster of Loch Ness is not a legend, but a fact.
sentences.zh: 尼斯湖水怪不是传说，而是事实。

sentences.en: Well, that's the kind of understated headline you would absolutely expect.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是那种你绝对会期待的轻描淡写的头条新闻。

sentences.en: So huge excitement.
sentences.zh: 所以人们极其兴奋。

sentences.en: And only once they've run the headline do they then send the prints to the Natural History Museum in London to see if they can identify it.
sentences.zh: 而且直到他们刊登了头条新闻之后，他们才把脚印送到伦敦自然历史博物馆，看是否能辨别出那是什么。

sentences.en: And what does the Natural History Museum say?
sentences.zh: 自然历史博物馆是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, they say that it is not the impression of any known aquatic mammal in the British Isles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们说这不是不列颠群岛任何已知水生哺乳动物的印记。

sentences.en: But they continue to do the research.
sentences.zh: 但他们继续进行研究。

sentences.en: And in the new year, so early 1934, they reveal that it is, in fact, a hippopotamus footprints.
sentences.zh: 到了新年，也就是1934年初，他们透露这实际上是河马的脚印。

sentences.en: And it's a single footprint.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个单独的脚印。

sentences.en: So in other words, it's a single footprint of a hippopotamus that has been pressed down into the mud over and over again to make it look like there are multiple footprints.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个河马脚印，被人一遍又一遍地按在泥里，好让人觉得有多个脚印。

sentences.en: And they suggest, the Natural History Museum suggests that it's a hunting trophy, a hippopotamus foot that's been converted into an umbrella stand,
sentences.zh: 他们暗示，自然历史博物馆暗示这是一个狩猎战利品，一个被改成伞架的河马脚，

sentences.en: which is very much the kind of thing that...
sentences.zh: 这非常符合那种……

sentences.en: That's such a 1930s story.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个极具20世纪30年代色彩的故事。

sentences.en: You kill a hippopotamus and you turn one of its legs into an umbrella stand.
sentences.zh: 你杀死了一只河马，然后把它的其中一条腿变成了一个伞架。

sentences.en: So I think this is a story that speaks very well of Marmaduke Weatherill, actually,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这个故事其实很能说明马马杜克·韦瑟里尔的问题，

sentences.en: because he is a man who clearly had the foresight to travel to Scotland with a hippopotamus foot umbrella stand in his luggage, just in case.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个显然有先见之明的人，在行李里带了一个河马脚伞架去苏格兰，以防万一。

sentences.en: Just in case.
sentences.zh: 以防万一。

sentences.en: Because he...
sentences.zh: 因为他……

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 说下去。

sentences.en: Well, but I think more probably it wasn't him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为更有可能不是他。

sentences.en: It was someone else who did it.
sentences.zh: 是别人做的。

sentences.en: Who was making fun of him.
sentences.zh: 在取笑他。

sentences.en: Knowing that he was looking.
sentences.zh: 明知他在寻找。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because, as we will find out, Weatherill is unbelievably upset by this.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们将要发现的，韦瑟里尔对此感到无比沮丧。

sentences.en: And he's particularly upset by the fact that the male, rather than standing by their man in his hour of need,
sentences.zh: 他尤其感到沮丧的是，《每日邮报》在他最需要的时候非但没有支持他，

sentences.en: turn on him and call him an idiot and mock him roundly for his incompetence.
sentences.zh: 反而调转枪口叫他笨蛋，并为他的无能对大肆嘲弄。

sentences.en: And again, goes all over the front page.
sentences.zh: 而且同样，这登上了各大头版。

sentences.en: I can't believe they would have done something like that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我真不敢相信他们会做出这种事，汤姆。

sentences.en: Shocking behavior and very unlike anything you get from it now.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的行为，这和现在的媒体风格大相径庭。

sentences.en: So Weatherill is left very, very embittered and with a big grudge against the male and against everybody involved in the search for Nessie.
sentences.zh: 所以韦瑟里尔感到非常非常痛苦，对《每日邮报》以及所有参与搜寻尼斯湖水怪的人怀恨在心。

sentences.en: So he withdraws, licking his wounds.
sentences.zh: 于是他退缩了，独自舔舐伤口。

sentences.en: But over the course of 1934, more and more extraordinary developments happen.
sentences.zh: 但在1934年的进程中，更多非凡的发展发生了。

sentences.en: So, and again, you get, you get people, the witnesses who cut through are witnesses who everyone can recognize as being reputable and reliable.
sentences.zh: 而且，你又会看到，那些引人注目的目击者都是每个人都认为声誉良好且可靠的目击者。

sentences.en: So early in January, you have a veterinary student on a motorbike who almost runs into the monster.
sentences.zh: 所以在1月上旬，有一个骑摩托车的兽医学生差点撞上怪物。

sentences.en: So Dominic, that's another one where the monster is out of the lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，这是又一个怪物跑到外面来的例子。

sentences.en: Out and about, rolling around.
sentences.zh: 出来到处走动，四处翻滚。

sentences.en: Doesn't, I mean, odd that it doesn't happen so much these days, but there you go.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，奇怪的是现在这种事不怎么发生了，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: And the veterinary student again says that it looks exactly like a plesiosaur.
sentences.zh: 那个兽医学生再次表示，它看起来跟蛇颈龙一模一样。

sentences.en: And then in April, you get probably the key piece of evidence and it's in the form of a photograph.
sentences.zh: 然后到了4月，你得到了可以说是最关键的证据，它是一张照片的形式。

sentences.en: And it's a much better photograph than the photograph that looks like a dog's head.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一张比那张看起来像狗头的照片好得多的照片。

sentences.en: And in fact, I would go so far as to say it's one of the most famous photographs of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我甚至可以说它是20世纪最著名的照片之一。

sentences.en: It's the photograph that everybody's seen.
sentences.zh: 这是每个人都见过的照片。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We'll publicize this podcast with.
sentences.zh: 我们将用它来宣传这个播客。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's, it looks like a plesiosaur.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来像一头蛇颈龙。

sentences.en: That's how you would describe it.
sentences.zh: 你会这么形容它。

sentences.en: It's a long neck creature with a hint of back and there are kind of ripples around it, black and white.
sentences.zh: 它是一个长颈生物，隐约露出背部，周围有一些涟漪，黑白的。

sentences.en: And you would know it if you've seen it.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过的话，你一眼就能认出来。

sentences.en: And this is known as the surgeon's photo.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“外科医生照片”。

sentences.en: It was taken in April, 1934.
sentences.zh: 它拍摄于1934年4月。

sentences.en: And it's called the surgeon's photo because the person who took it was both a surgeon, but didn't want to be named.
sentences.zh: 之所以被称为“外科医生照片”，是因为拍下它的人既是一名外科医生，又不想透露姓名。

sentences.en: And again, this reticence was seen as something that suggested that, you know, the accuracy of it because he clearly wasn't after publicity.
sentences.zh: 同样，这种缄默被视为表明其准确性的一点，你知道的，因为他显然不是为了出名。

sentences.en: He's not after publicity.
sentences.zh: 他不是为了出名。

sentences.en: And it turns out, so the surgeon is a man called Robert Wilson, who's a gynecologist, has rooms off Harley Street.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，这位外科医生是一个名叫罗伯特·威尔逊的人，他是一名妇科医生，在哈雷街附近有诊所。

sentences.en: And the whole, I mean, again, this is another character who seems sprung from a Buchan novel.
sentences.zh: 而且整件事情——我是说，这也是另一个仿佛从巴肯的小说里走出来的人物。

sentences.en: The kind of the hint of tales of imperial daring do.
sentences.zh: 带着帝国无畏冒险故事的暗示。

sentences.en: So he is born in Madagascar.
sentences.zh: 所以他出生在马达加斯加。

sentences.en: He's the son of missionaries.
sentences.zh: 他是传教士的儿子。

sentences.en: He goes to boarding school in England.
sentences.zh: 他在英格兰上寄宿学校。

sentences.en: He comes of age during the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他在第一次世界大战期间成年。

sentences.en: The day that he becomes of age, he rushes off, enlists, serves very valiantly and well in the First World War, gets mentioned in dispatches, comes back,
sentences.zh: 就在他成年的那天，他冲了出去，应征入伍，在一战中英勇作战，战功显赫，受到嘉奖，然后回来，

sentences.en: sets up his medical practice.
sentences.zh: 开办了他的诊所。

sentences.en: And he is the person who produces this photo.
sentences.zh: 而他就是拍下这张照片的人。

sentences.en: So, and the Daily Mail get hold of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，《每日邮报》拿到了这张照片。

sentences.en: They cop it to make it look as impressive as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们对其进行了剪裁，使其看起来尽可能震撼。

sentences.en: They put it on the front page.
sentences.zh: 他们把它放在了头版。

sentences.en: And really, that's the photograph that makes it not just a global, a national talking point, but a global talking point.
sentences.zh: 说真的，正是这张照片让它不仅成为了一个全国性的谈资，也成为了一个全球性的谈资。
